topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening topic introduces the lecturer, course outline, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutation versus Environmental and Genetic Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step nature of cancer development, evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic biological bad luck, inherited genetic risk, and environmental exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents drive cancer development, detailing the environmental co-factors and molecular pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and dietary or inhaled chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammatory Microenvironments, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how non-mutagenic factors such as chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and developmental tissue states facilitate cancer outgrowth, ending with a mechanistic summary.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to demonstrate carcinogenicity and identify mutational signatures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing topic summarizes the challenges in determining carcinogenic potency and concludes the lecture with reflections on balancing everyday risks and benefits.
